My Experience as a Tenant: Severe Mismanagement and Water Crisis
- I have lived here as a tenant for over a year, and it has been a highly frustrating experience due to severe water mismanagement. Water shortages occur every few months and last for days. Instead of proactive planning, updates are inconsistent, and residents are routinely left without water for 10–12 hours at a stretch. Basic necessities are ignored; for instance, water was cut overnight just to host a Holi festival rain dance the next morning.The root cause appears to be severe internal conflict between the old and new management committees. The current committee blames the previous one instead of taking responsibility (they'll behave and show as if there's no issue but I have spoken to some of flat owners here who have themselves admitted that there is a huge conflict within the society members due to which all the mismanagement happens). This political infighting leads to massive confusion, poor decision-making, and an absolute inability to handle basic utility crisis. Tenants who raise concerns are dismissed as immature and naive or told to leave.This complex is wrongly marketed as a "premium" society. A premium property is defined by competent management, transparency, and crisis handling—not just basic amenities. They only encourage tenant's participation during festival celebrations and other society events and ask for monetary contributions. Rest of the times, during water crisis, tenants are not given much information and told, "Don't become a water warden". The only positive aspect is the physical infrastructure. The builder created a beautiful, spacious property, but good construction cannot compensate for broken management. I strongly advise prospective residents to do thorough due diligence before renting or purchasing a flat here- it might save your precious time and money.

featured_reviews.name: Neha Shungloo
featured_reviews.review_text:
Worst place to live - have been here for 3 years almost now can’t wait to leave. The residents have no civic sense- they are throwing kitchen waste out of the window and dirty sanitary napkins in common areas from bathroom vent areas - children take a shit in the pool - my staff quarters entire roof caved in on my staffs head - if someone on the 1st floor is drilling a hole you can hear it all the way upto to the 21st floor - the walls are thin and useless

There are so many wild rabid stray dogs that I can’t take my cat out for walks and my dogs have been getting sick every 3 months - I’ve lived in Bombay for 10years now and never have my dogs ever gotten so sick as they have because of the filth this society allows to fester.
The pigeons are a massive problem - the lobby area they connects to the central section sense of Theo shit and piss no matter what you do - the other day a Pigeon was hanging dead right outside my balcony after getting caught in some decorations my upstairs neighbour had put up.

We can’t even sit in the balcony because the hawks attack and try to steal your food.

I feel sorry for the housekeeping staff - they clean 3 times a day but with such terrible civic sense there’s only so much they can do.

Let me also add the people leave the lifts smelling like labourers went through. Body odour seems to be the fragrance of Sam. It’s nauseating & the gym just smells like sweat and despair. The only good thing about the place is the breeze in the evening but with the dust, traffic noise and sneak of human waste coming from right outside even that is ruined.

featured_reviews.name: Nazish Siddiqui
featured_reviews.review_text:
Dear Lodha Bel Air Team,
There is no doubt that the location of the property and its surrounding connectivity are excellent. The open spaces and greenery within the project are also commendable and greatly appreciated.
However, I am writing to express my disappointment regarding the construction quality, materials, and accessories used in the property. We are already facing issues such as leakage and signs of poor construction, which are unacceptable from a reputed developer like Lodha.
I was seriously considering investing in your upcoming project in the same area. However, given the current experience, I am now hesitant and concerned about facing similar issues in the future.
I sincerely hope that these problems will be addressed promptly and professionally. A positive resolution would certainly help restore confidence and allow me to consider future investments with Lodha.
Nazish Siddiqui
F1604
